evidence: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534,537,554,557,576,579 call r.log.Error on every batch of the normal cleanup loop, even when err is nil (they log 'Annotations to clean', 'cleaned annotations', etc.). These look like debugging leftovers. They would flood error logs and set off error alerting on every cleanup cycle. They should be Debug, or removed. The caller cleanup.go:127 already logs the outcome at Debug level.

xorm_store.go:534,554,576 log "ids", ids, which is the full slice for each batch. The batch size comes from cleanupjob_batchsize (setting.go:710, default 100, but users can set it much higher). cleanup_test.go:101 tests a batch size of 32767, so a single log line could hold tens of thousands of IDs. Logging only the count (already present) is enough. This would be resolved together with issue 0.

xorm_store.go:609-612 builds the ID list with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v). This reallocates and copies the whole string on every step, so it is O(n^2). The path only runs on SQLite when batch size > 999 (line 608), and it runs once per batch, so the real impact is small next to the DB round trip. strings.Builder or strconv plus strings.Join would be cleaner and linear. This is a low-priority improvement.

xorm_store.go:605-607 says 'SQLite has a parameter limit of 999'. Since SQLite 3.32.0, SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER defaults to 32766, not the 32767 the reviewer stated. go.mod:81 pins mattn/go-sqlite3 v1.14.16, which bundles SQLite 3.39.x, so the bundled build already has the higher limit. Using 999 is still a safe, conservative threshold: it only switches to inlined integer IDs, which is correct either way. So the code is fine and only the comment is misleading. Clarifying that 999 is for compatibility with older or custom builds is a doc-only fix.

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 changes the ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute. The reviewer's mechanism is wrong. srv.clean(ctx) runs synchronously inside the select loop (cleanup.go:78-81), and a Go time.Ticker channel buffers one tick and drops the rest, so cleanup runs cannot overlap or run concurrently. The 9-minute timeout (cleanup.go:89) just limits each run. The change itself is still a real problem. It is not mentioned in the PR description, it looks like a debugging leftover (like the log.Error calls), and it makes all 8 cleanup jobs run 10x as often, back to back whenever a run takes more than a minute. That adds DB load and more chances for the very lock contention this PR is trying to reduce. It should be reverted to time.Minute * 10.
